function: Joint design of BS precoder and RIS phase shifts maximizing weighted sum spectral efficiency, using two small NNs fed with gradients and optimized per channel (p. 3-5).
system: mmWave downlink MU-MISO: 64-antenna BS, 4 single-antenna users, passive reflecting RIS with 100 elements, 28 GHz, direct links blocked (p. 3, 6-7).
method: Gradient-based meta learning: precoding and theta networks (200-neuron hidden layer) take gradients as input; self-supervised loss, Adam, no pre-training; precoder compressed to K by K (p. 4-7).
data_channel: Simulated Rician fading (factor 10) with 3GPP TS 36.814 path loss for main results; 3GPP TS 36.814 and TS 36.885 generated channels for dynamic scenarios (p. 6-7, 10).
test_conditions: No pre-training: NNs randomly initialized and optimized per channel sample (100 samples, 500 epochs); sweeps of power, N, M, CEE; dynamic scenarios at 0, 60, 120 km/h (p. 7-10).
baselines: Random phase with WMMSE; AO [10]; DNN of [42]; variants GML and ML without manifold learning or gradient input (p. 7).
metrics: Spectral efficiency versus power, RIS size, antennas, epochs, CEE and time slots; CPU time; epochs to surpass AO (p. 7-10).
complexity: O(Ne No Ni K^2 M N), Table III; CPU time 4.7 s versus 108.1 s for AO at M=256, N=160 (p. 6-8).
q1_support: p. 10: "Technical standards [41] and [43] are separately used to generate perfect channel data for stationary and moving scenarios." These are 3GPP TS 36.814 and TS 36.885 (p. 12). The main results use Rician fading with only the path loss from 3GPP (p. 6: "the path loss is established based on the 3GPP propagation environment standard [41]"), which alone would not count.
q2_support: p. 10: "the embedded NNs are updated within each channel optimization, but are randomly initialized across each channel realization." Every channel, sweep point and scenario is optimized from scratch, so no trained model is carried to new conditions; only the DNN baseline is adapted (five adaptation channels per slot).
q3_support: p. 7: "Baseline 4 (DNN): The deep learning model in [42] is adopted" and "Baseline 5 (AO): The traditional optimization method in [10] is adopted"; p. 7: "4.11% and 7.31% higher performance than AO and DNN" on spectral efficiency at 10 dBm.
q4_support: p. 6: "The complexity of GMML has been proven to be O(Ne No Ni K 2 M N )"; p. 8: "the AO algorithm takes 108.1 seconds to converge, while the GMML algorithm only takes 4.7 seconds".
q5_support: p. 2: "The code for this paper is available online in [35]." p. 12: reference [35] gives "https:// github.com/ fenghaozhu/ GMML", that is, https://github.com/fenghaozhu/GMML.
notes: Included in area 3 with a passive reflecting RIS of 100 elements; the NNs are trained by Adam on the spectral-efficiency loss inside each channel (self-supervised, no pre-training), a learned component. q1 is marked 1 only for the dynamic scenarios generated with 3GPP TS 36.814 and TS 36.885, standardized models outside the listed ones; the main results are a custom Rician simulator with 3GPP path loss, so the reviewer should confirm. q2 is 0 because the NNs restart from random initialization for every channel, although the dynamic-scenario test exists (p. 10).
